clue.text: Edge forward, in preparation to kill

parts.note: a hem is the folded edge of a garment
a lock is a forward in the second row of a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A fighter edges forward, readying for the kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' reads as a verb of motion; it is the noun, a rugby forward. The poison is the one Socrates drank.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a poisonous plant whose extract was the classic deadly potion, so a lethal preparation.

clue.text: No good slicing meat and not finishing game

indicators.note: no good slices into the meat

parts.note: ham is cured pork
NG, abbreviation for no good

indicators.note: the word and stops short of its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone no good at carving meat abandons a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangman is a word-guessing game played with pencil and paper.

clue.text: One removing bombs digs with blade and runs

annotationWithheld.why: One removing bombs digs with blade and runs: the parse MINES + W + EEPE (EPEE reversed) + R needs a reversal the printed clue never signals (blog notes the missing indicator), so no honest parse
annotationWithheld.clue: One removing bombs digs with blade and runs

clue.text: Cricket side with number performing well

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
a number is a song in a show

explanation.surface: A cricket team with a numbers man is playing well.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on (or leg) side is the half of the field by the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on song is a British idiom for being in top form.

clue.text: Back-to back defeats in a couple of cups upset rugby winger in Australia

parts.note: KO, a knockout, set back to back with its own reversal

indicators.note: the reversed rugby letters go inside the cups word

parts.note: a bra has two cups

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so backwards

parts.note: RU, Rugby Union

explanation.surface: After two straight defeats in cup matches, a rugby winger in Australia is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RU into UR, which goes 'in' BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The kookaburra is a large Australian kingfisher, so a bird, a winged creature.

clue.text: Papers back man giving female stick

indicators.note: back tells us the papers abbreviation is read from its end

parts.note: ID, identity papers
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Newspapers support a man who gives a woman a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ID into DI. The definition combines the two senses: the spinning stick, and the female side of a family (the distaff side).
explanation.definitionFit: A distaff is the rod used in hand spinning, traditionally women's work, hence also an adjective meaning female.

clue.text: Dawdlers wouldn't touch Scotch

definitions.meaning: people who dawdle would never hurry off
to scotch a plan is to put an end to it

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition; 'Scotch' looks like whisky but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means a sprint, a tiny amount, and to wreck hopes.

clue.text: One held by the scruff — a state to behold!

indicators.note: the one letter is held by, placed next to, the scruff

parts.note: a sloven is a scruffy, untidy person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed by the scruff of the neck is a sight to behold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruff' suggests the back of the neck; it is a scruffy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a European country, and a state in the political sense.

clue.text: For mountain climbing map mostly required

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the letters upwards
mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: To climb a mountain you need most of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, especially in Switzerland.

clue.text: Now opposing, perhaps, as never previously

definitions.meaning: someone usually against who is now in favour is in favour this time
on this one occasion, unlike before

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on 'for' meaning in favour: a habitual opponent now 'for', once.
explanation.definitionFit: For once means on this occasion only, unusually.

clue.text: Bread in a nutritious sandwich

indicators.note: the run of letters is sandwiched within the words in a nutritious

explanation.surface: Bread inside a healthy sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but its last letter starts the run, which ends at the first letter of 'nutritious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a flat leavened Indian bread, here in its alternative spelling.

clue.text: Hat being put on proves a sensational act

indicators.note: the hat is put on, placed after, the word for proves

parts.note: to show something is to prove it
a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Putting on a hat shows that the act is a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a performance so good the audience's applause halts the show.

clue.text: Jam Nora's put specially in this container

indicators.note: the letters are put together specially, in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Nora puts her jam in a special jar.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of JAM NORAS are rearranged; 'put' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason jar is a glass preserving jar with a screw lid, the very thing for jam.

clue.text: Mice maybe see stoat with no tail

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: the stoat's word loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: an ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: Mice may spot a stoat that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are an example of pests, small destructive animals regarded as vermin.

clue.text: Unruly mob quiz a man of African origin

indicators.note: unruly says the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: An unruly crowd quizzes a man from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mozambiquan comes from Mozambique, a country in southeast Africa.

clue.text: Schoolboy showing why mistake corrected

indicators.note: corrected says the letters are put right, into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy explains why a mistake has been corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wykehamist attends Winchester College, an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wykehamist is a pupil of Winchester College, founded by William of Wykeham.

clue.text: Opponents interfere in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to nose is to pry or interfere

explanation.surface: Opponents interfere when someone is giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The noes are those voting against a motion, the opposing side.

clue.text: Plant making copper ruler in diminutive form

parts.note: a busy is old slang for a policeman or detective
Lizzie is a pet form of Elizabeth, a name borne by queens

explanation.surface: A plant turns a policeman into a little ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy lizzie is the common name of impatiens, a popular flowering house and bedding plant.

clue.text: They've got out fresh cases packed with soft drugs

indicators.note: the rearranged cases are packed with the other letters
fresh says the letters of cases are made new, rearranged

parts.note: P, piano, soft in music
E is ecstasy; two of them are drugs

explanation.surface: Escaped prisoners pack fresh cases with soft drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes ESCAS from CASES, and PEE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapees are people who have broken free from confinement.

clue.text: Recorded evidence heard in court containing much embroidery

parts.note: tapes are recordings used in evidence
a case heard in court is tried

explanation.surface: Taped evidence is heard by a court in a case about needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' suggests a sound-alike, but here it is the legal sense of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapestried is hung or worked with tapestry, a heavily embroidered-looking woven fabric.

clue.text: Strudel's ideal regularly served with variable date portion, sometimes

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting from the second

parts.note: Y, a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Strudel is regularly served on a certain day, sometimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday name is often part of a written date, as in a heading.

clue.text: Winter festival marks cracking return of jazz player

indicators.note: the marks letter cracks open the reversed word
return of says the player's word is read backwards

parts.note: sax, short for saxophone
M, abbreviation for the old German mark

explanation.surface: At a winter festival, marks are cracking as the jazz player returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns SAX into XAS, and 'cracking' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is the common short written form of Christmas, the December festival.

clue.text: Shaken with whistling, son will end disheartened

parts.note: S, abbreviation for son
a will is a wish

indicators.note: the word end loses its heart, its middle letter

explanation.surface: Shaken and whistling, a son wants things to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail or cane swished is moved with a whistling sound through the air.

clue.text: Sing and shake hands on welcoming Queen

indicators.note: the deal word welcomes, takes in, the queen

parts.note: to seal a deal is to shake hands on it
QU, abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Sing and shake hands to welcome the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' is criminal slang for informing, like squeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal, like to sing, is slang for informing on accomplices.

clue.text: Potentially deafening build-up late around war torn area

indicators.note: the word for late goes around the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former, as late does

indicators.note: torn says the letters of war are ripped apart and rearranged

parts.note: A, abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A deafening noise builds up late in a war-torn area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially deafening build-up' reads like rising noise; it describes the substance clogging the ear. 'torn' rearranges WAR, and 'around' has EX enclose the result plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax accumulating in the ear canal can block it and dull the hearing.

clue.text: Contents from liquid drip on lawyer's cocktail

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the inner letters follow the lawyer

parts.note: DA, district attorney, an American lawyer

indicators.note: the contents are the inner letters of each word, without their ends

explanation.surface: Liquid drips on to a lawyer's cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Inner letters of 'liquid' and 'drip' give IQUI and RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A daiquiri is a rum cocktail with lime juice and sugar.

clue.text: Old dictator's claim to popularity

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as AM IN, as in 'I am in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idi Amin was Uganda's military dictator; AM IN claims being in favour.

clue.text: Would ultimately not like cats outside small room in town

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of would
the phrase for not like cats goes outside the abbreviated room

parts.note: feline means like a cat, so unfeline means not catlike
RM, abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes cats would stay outside a small room in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter invents an adjective, 'unfeline', for 'not like cats'. 'Would ultimately' supplies D, and 'outside' wraps that invented word round RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunfermline is a town in Fife, Scotland, once its royal capital.

clue.text: Love unravelling Times' clues, taking seconds only

indicators.note: only the second letter of each word is taken; the reversed run inside the first word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Love unravels when solving the newspaper's clues, needing only seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means zero in tennis scoring, a score of nothing.

clue.text: About-turn by pair before I can make expression of revulsion

parts.note: a U-turn is an about-turn
G and H come just before I in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A turnaround by a couple makes someone exclaim in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair before I' sounds like a couple ahead of the speaker; it means the alphabet's two letters before I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugh is an interjection uttered in disgust.

clue.text: Russian leader, however wrong, adopting line

indicators.note: the word for however takes in the line letter

parts.note: yet means however, nevertheless
L, abbreviation for line
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A Russian leader, however wrong, takes up a party line.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of the Russian Federation.

clue.text: Clawed and bit, eating like a wolf?

indicators.note: the small word eats, takes inside, the other

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
a lone wolf operates by itself

explanation.surface: An animal clawed and bit, eating like a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a wolf' suggests ravenous eating; it is the lone wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Taloned means having talons, sharp claws, so equipped with claws.
